Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) signs MoU with TRIFED to Strengthen Market Access for PM Vishwakarma Artisans
articles.full_content:
TRIFED to facilitate onboarding, capacity building, product promotion and market access through Tribes India retail outlets and its online marketplace Collaboration to establish a “Tribes India–PM Vishwakarma Collection” and expand the visibility of products made by artisans
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, to strengthen market access for eligible tribal artisans registered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. The MoU was signed in the presence of Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME; Shri M. Raja Murugan, Managing Director, TRIFED; along with Shri Nitish Kumar, Deputy Director General (DDG); Shri Danish Ashraf, Joint Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME; and Shri Prateek Singh Meena, Executive Director, TRIFED. The collaboration brings together the Ministry of MSME’s PM Vishwakarma framework and TRIFED’s established Tribes India marketplace and retail network.
The PM Vishwakarma Scheme, launched on 17 September 2023, seeks to improve the quality and reach of the products and services of traditional artisans and craftspeople. The Scheme supports artisans whose skills are passed from generation to generation through the traditional guru-shishya model of training within families and informal groups.
Objectives of the MoU :-
• Under the MoU, the Ministry of MSME and TRIFED will collaborate to facilitate the display, promotion and sale of products made by eligible tribal artisans registered under PM Vishwakarma scheme. The collaboration will cover product-based trades such as carpenter, metalsmith, sculptor, goldsmith, potter, shoe smith, basket, mat /broom maker/ coir weaver, doll and toy maker, garland maker, etc.
• TRIFED will facilitate the onboarding and capacity building of eligible tribal artisans referred by the Ministry of MSME and provide them market access through the Tribes India retail network and its online marketplace, subject to applicable onboarding conditions and policies.
• Products made by participating tribal artisans will be displayed through the Tribes India retail network and on tribesindia.com under the proposed “Tribes India–PM Vishwakarma Collection”, subject to sellers’ consent and compliance with applicable TRIFED policies.
• TRIFED will facilitate aggregation, quality assurance and packaging support for market-ready products and will work with the Ministry of MSME to provide initial product imaging and cataloguing support to mutually identified sellers.
• TRIFED will facilitate promotion of products made by identified tribal Vishwakarmas through its e-marketplace and provide dedicated display and sales space across its outlets, subject to the provisions and applicable terms of the MoU.

SEEPZ-SEZ strengthens Green Energy Infrastructure; Electricity Tariff reduced from ₹8.65 to ₹5.60 per unit
articles.full_content:
Santacruz Electronic Export Processing Zone (SEEPZ-SEZ) has achieved 100% green electricity supply and delivered savings of ₹32.5 crore in electricity costs to its consumers during FY 2025–26, marking a significant step towards sustainable industrial development and enhanced export competitiveness.
The revised tariff benefits 243 units and other utilities, covering a total of 495 electricity consumers operating in the Jewellery, Electronics and IT sectors. Under the Adani Electricity SEEPZ Limited (ASL) tariff structure, the electricity rate within the zone is ₹5.60 per unit, compared to ₹8.65 per unit outside the zone.
The tariff reduction follows the efforts of the SEEPZ-SEZ Authority to strengthen the power distribution framework by bringing Adani Electricity SEEPZ Limited (ASL) on board as a co-developer. The new distribution framework became operational on 1st November 2023. Under this arrangement, ASL has been supplying 100% green electricity to the zone since July 2026. Earlier, in January 2025, following representations by the SEEPZ-SEZ Authority and the SEEPZ Gems and Jewellery Association (SGJMA), the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) approved the revised tariff, which came into effect from 1st April 2025.
The savings are expected to increase further, with annual savings projected to reach ₹54 crore by FY 2029–30 at current consumption levels.
Expanding Solar Power
The SEEPZ-SEZ Authority has also installed solar power plants at the Mega Common Facility Centre (CFC) and NEST-1. Solar infrastructure is being further extended to NEST-2 and the rooftops of other buildings across SEEPZ.
Strengthening Power Infrastructure
The zone's distribution system comprises 48 substations with an aggregate capacity of 53 MVA and approximately 30 km of underground cabling. This infrastructure supports a power demand of around 35–40 MW, ensuring reliable power supply with minimal interruptions. ASL is planning to implement Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC)-approved Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), while additional substations are being developed to improve grid resilience and strengthen energy security for supplying green energy to every unit in SEEPZ.
With the SEEPZ 2.0 redevelopment expected to increase the zone's power requirement to 70–80 MW, the SEEPZ-SEZ Authority is planning to augment its electrical infrastructure in parallel with upcoming developments, including NEST-3, to ensure reliable, affordable and green power for future growth.The initiative reflects the SEEPZ-SEZ Authority's commitment to making Indian exports greener, more cost-competitive and globally resilient.
Edgar Coelho / Madhura Nerurkar

BRE Summit & Expo 2026 Reinforces India’s Position as a Major Global Force in Renewable Energy: Union New & Renewable Energy Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi
articles.full_content:
The Summit reinforces India's position as a resilient clean-energy economy, an attractive investment destination and a global partner for sustainable development: Shri Joshi
India has emerged as a major global force in renewable energy, with the world taking notice of its progress and growing ambitions, said Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, while addressing the media at the conclusion of the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit 2026 here today.
He said that Bharat Mandapam had brought together global policymakers, investors, industry leaders and innovators from across the world. With participation from more than 135 countries, the Summit emerged as one of India's largest global platforms for renewable energy. He noted that this was the first time that three important events in the renewable energy sector had been held together, with overwhelming participation from domestic and international stakeholders demonstrating global confidence in India's renewable energy growth story.
The Summit was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 2 nd November 2026. In his address, the Prime Minister highlighted the strategic importance of India's sustained investments in renewable energy in strengthening the country's resilience to global disruptions, arising from COVID-19 pandemic and the West Asia crisis. He observed that India’s investment in the renewable energy sector has largely shielded the country from these disruptions.
The Prime Minister underscored that India's renewable energy journey is not only transforming its domestic energy landscape but also generating solutions and experiences that can benefit the world. Emphasising India's commitment to sharing its innovations and achievements with humanity, he highlighted the potential of India's clean energy success to support the energy transition in countries across the world. Calling for greater participation in the clean energy innovation ecosystem, the Prime Minister invited startups, IITs, innovators and entrepreneurs to develop solutions and business models through which an increasing number of household energy requirements can be met using clean energy.
Organised from 2 nd -5 th November, the four-day summit brought together global policymakers, industry leaders, investors, technology providers, researchers, startups and international institutions on a common platform to advance the clean energy transition. The Summit witnessed strong participation with over 75000 visitors, 400 plus exhibitors and more than 627 speakers across 113 sessions, with representation from 135 countries with about 800 delegates, including the Partner countries, ISA members, International Organisations, and Diplomatic Missions located in India. High-level ministerial participation included 32 international Ministers, 6 Chief Ministers and 10 State Energy Ministers, reflecting strong engagement from both national and sub-nationa

Telangana Pollution Control Board Conducts Awareness-cum-Training Programme on Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
articles.full_content:
The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) conducted an Awareness-cum-Hands-on Training Programme on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, on November 5, 2026, at Paryavarana Bhavan, Sanathnagar, Hyderabad. Organised in hybrid mode, the programme aimed to familiarise the concerned Government Departments, District Collectors, and Urban and Rural Local Bodies with their respective statutory roles and responsibilities under the Rules and provide practical guidance on using the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) Centralised Online Solid Waste Management (SWM) Portal (https://swmp.cpcb.gov.in).
The training session was conducted by Smt. M. Sujana Sree, Senior Environmental Engineer, TGPCB, State Nodal Officer for the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and designated State Master Trainer, under the supervision of the Member Secretary, TGPCB.
The programme covered the statutory responsibilities of the Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department (MA&UD), Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department (PR&RD), District Collectors, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Rural Local Bodies (RLBs), Gram Panchayats (GPs) and Bulk Waste Generators (BWGs).
A detailed walkthrough of the CPCB Centralised Online SWM Portal was followed by practical, hands-on demonstrations of its features and workflows. The demonstrations covered the complete registration and onboarding processes for UDD, ULBs, RDD, Gram Panchayats and BWGs, including user creation, application submission and verification, data entry, facility registration, geo-tagging, inspection-related functions, annual returns, Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) certificates, appeals, grievance redressal and other relevant portal functionalities.
Participants were guided through the respective login procedures, responsibilities and actions required at each stage to enable them to independently carry out the portal-related processes. The training also covered the roles of the concerned departments and authorities in coordinating and monitoring the implementation of the Rules, reporting compliance and maintaining relevant information through the Centralised Online Portal.
Officials from Hyderabad, Rangareddy and Medchal–Malkajgiri districts participated in person, while officials from the remaining districts joined the programme online. Representatives of the concerned State Government Departments also attended the programme in person.

Organised in hybrid mode, the programme aimed to familiarise the concerned Government Departments, District Collectors, and Urban and Rural Local Bodies with their respective statutory roles and responsibilities under the Rules and provide practical guidance on using the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) Centralised Online Solid Waste Management (SWM) Portal (https://swmp.cpcb.gov.in). articles.title: Vice President of India Honours the Ministry of Railways with the PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award
articles.full_content:
12,495 Railway Buildings Equipped with Rooftop Solar Systems Across the Country 351 MW of Rooftop Solar Capacity Commissioned by Railway Ministry
Hon’ble Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, honoured the Ministry of Railways with the prestigious PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award today at the Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026, held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
The Ministry secured the top position in the category of “Maximum Buildings Solarized by Central Ministries/Departments” under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, setting an inspiring national benchmark for renewable energy adoption across public institutions.
The Ministry has identified 15,868 feasible railway buildings across the country for rooftop solar installations. So far, 12,495 buildings, accounting for 79% of the total identified buildings, have been equipped with rooftop solar systems. The Ministry has also commissioned 351 MW of rooftop solar capacity against its target of 424 MW.
At the national level, 25,984 of the 39,135 buildings identified across 77 Central Ministries and Departments have been solarized so far, accounting for 66% of the total identified buildings. The Ministry of Railways has contributed a significant share to this nationwide achievement.
The Ministry of Railways remains committed to solarizing all remaining feasible buildings by March 2027, reinforcing its commitment to a clean, energy-efficient and sustainable future for India.
Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Vanshita Jaiswal

NITI Aayog and GIZ India Sign Implementation Agreement under Nationally Determined Contribution-Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) to Accelerate Road Freight Decarbonisation
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) on 3 rd November 2026. NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government's International Climate Initiative (IKI). World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India and Agora Energiewende are among the initiative's implementing partners.
Decarbonising road freight is an important component of India's transition towards a sustainable, energy-efficient and low-carbon transport system. However, the electrification of medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles remains at an early stage, highlighting the need for adequate charging infrastructure, innovative financing mechanisms and an enabling regulatory framework. The Agreement formalises the collaboration between the project partners for accelerating the decarbonisation of India's road freight sector. The initiative will contribute to India's broader efforts to achieve its Nationally Determined Contribution targets and long-term climate goals.
articles.summary: NITI Aayog and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) on 3 rd November 2026. NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government's International Climate Initiative (IKI). World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India and Agora Energiewende are among the initiative's implementing partners.

PM Surya Ghar Has Truly Transformed into a Mass Movement: Shri Pralhad Joshi
articles.full_content:
Five Country Partners deepen bilateral clean energy ties across hydrogen, offshore wind and financing BRE Summit and Expo 2026 Charts India’s Technology-Led Clean Energy Future
“The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has truly transformed into a mass movement, ultimately ensuring welfare and savings for the people, the states, and the entire country”, said Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi at a fireside chat during the 3 rd day of a Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 here today.
Union Minister Shri Joshi highlighted that India is now completing approximately one lakh rooftop solar installations every six days because of the rooftop solar initiative. He noted that this is not only reducing emissions but also strengthening India's energy security during peak hours. Emphasising the tangible benefits, he stated that millions of households are achieving zero electricity bills and generating substantial collective income by selling surplus power back to the grid. He further highlighted India's exponential growth in solar energy, with installed capacity increasing from a mere 3 GW in 2014 to 172 GW today.
The Next Terawatt Diplomatic Dialogue, addressed by Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, underscored that the next terawatt of clean energy will require collective collaboration across countries, technologies and institutions. The minister also sought the views of the diplomats on country partnerships, investment, technology, implementation and capacity building.
A parallel CEO Caucus convened by the International Solar Alliance, CEEW and Energiva Ventures mapped the international clean energy implementation architecture for the decades ahead, with the ISA High-Level Assembly and a SIDS Ministerial Roundtable adding further diplomatic weight. Country sessions with Norway, Japan, Australia, the United Kingdom and France deepened bilateral ties across hydrogen, offshore wind and financing, while Karnataka, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh each presented their renewable energy investment pipelines to a global audience.
The 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen, held alongside BRE Summit and Expo 2026, highlighted progress under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, which targets 5 million tonnes of annual green hydrogen production capacity by 2030. Sessions across the day examined electrolyser manufacturing, hydrogen in mobility, fuel cell technologies and sustainable aviation fuels, reinforcing India’s hydrogen economy as a key pillar of the broader energy transition.
Industry leaders, researchers, manufacturers and knowledge partners are using the platform to explore technology collaborations, research partnerships and opportunities to strengthen domestic supply chains.

IICA signs MoU with IAMC to augment Alternative Dispute Resolution ecosystem and facilitate Ease of Doing Business in India
articles.full_content:
Collaboration to focus on specialized capacity building, MSME mediation support, policy-oriented research, and advancing India’s ADR framework towards Viksit Bharat@2047
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) signed an MOU with the International Arbitration and Mediation Centre (IAMC), Hyderabad, an autonomous institution established with the support of the Government of Telangana and the High Court of Telangana. The MOU marks a significant step towards strengthening institutional collaboration and promoting professional excellence in arbitration, mediation, corporate affairs and related areas of mutual interest.
Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director-General & CEO, IICA, welcomed Shri AJ Jawad, CEO & Registrar, IAMC, and in their presence the MoU was signed by Shri Col. Amandeep Singh Puri, Chief Administrative Officer, IICA and Shri AJ Jawad, CEO & Registrar, IAMC.
Prof. (Dr.) Naveen Sirohi, Head, Centre for Excellence in Alternative Dispute Resolution (CEADR), IICA welcomed the dignitaries and highlighted the importance of institutional partnerships in fostering knowledge exchange, professional development and collaborative initiatives.
In his Keynote Address, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh laid emphasis on the importance of collaboration between IICA & IAMC towards the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 for creating a specialized pool of arbitrators, mediators and dispute resolution professionals through customised short-term and long-term courses, workshops, seminars and other skill development programs.
He stressed the importance of mediation in the MSME sector considering its linkages with economic growth, GDP, exports and envisaged deepening of sectoral focus by the two institutions. Further, regional support to the vision of the state of Haryana like Trillion-Dollar Economy by 2047 may be considered which may not be possible without investors' confidence driven by strong institutional arbitration and mediation centre.
Shri AJ Jawad, in his Special Address, highlighted that IAMC looks forward to working closely with IICA to leverage each other’s institutional expertise and resources for developing structured programmes, joint initiatives, and policy-oriented research that would augment and strengthen the ADR ecosystem in India. He stated that the MoU aligns with the broader vision of enhancing professional excellence, promoting best practices, and fostering innovation in arbitration, mediation, and dispute resolution training and institutional development.
The MoU Signing was organized by the Centre of Excellence in Alternative Dispute Resolution (CEADR) under the guidance of Prof (Dr) Naveen Sirohi, Head, School of Finance & Management & Centre of Excellence in Alternative Dispute Resolution.
